Terms are correct and consistent (vector de estado, medición en la base estándar, equivalentes salvo una fase global, ley de los grandes números), the numbers in [35] (5 of 9, about 556 of 1000) match the English, and the tú register holds. The one thing to change is in [0], where the lesson name "single-systems" becomes "sistemas de un solo elemento". That phrase reads like "one-element systems" rather than "a single system", so "sistemas individuales" or "sistemas simples" would be better.

examples.source: Using Qiskit to implement ideas from the single-systems lesson.
examples.translation: Uso de Qiskit para implementar las ideas de la lección sobre sistemas de un solo elemento.
examples.suggested: Uso de Qiskit para implementar las ideas de la lección sobre sistemas individuales.

editor_note: In entry [34], the Spanish Eastin-Knill theorem drops "generates". The English says the set of transversal logical gates generates a discrete set of operations. The Spanish says the set of gates itself "es discreto". That turns the theorem into a false inference, since a discrete gate set such as {H, T} can still generate a universal set, so a learner would come away with the wrong idea of why transversal gates fail. There are also three smaller losses of nuance: [59] drops "just" ("no necesitamos estados mágicos"), [60] drops the caveat "selected to make it so", and [61] turns "perhaps more accurately" into a flat "más precisamente". Terminology (puerta, qubit, código estabilizador, destilación de estados mágicos) and the tú register are otherwise sound and consistent.

examples.source: the set of logical gates that can be implemented transversally generates a set of operations that (up to a global phase) is discrete, and is therefore not universal.
examples.translation: el conjunto de puertas lógicas que pueden implementarse de forma transversal es discreto (salvo un factor de fase global) y, por lo tanto, no es universal.
examples.suggested: el conjunto de puertas lógicas que pueden implementarse de forma transversal genera un conjunto de operaciones que (salvo un factor de fase global) es discreto y, por lo tanto, no es universal.
examples.why: Dropping 'genera' makes the theorem claim that the gate set is discrete, not the group it generates. A discrete gate set can still be universal, so the 'por lo tanto' no longer follows and the learner is taught the wrong reason.

examples.source: we actually don't need just magic states — we need *encoded* magic states.
examples.translation: en realidad no necesitamos estados mágicos — necesitamos estados mágicos *codificados*.
examples.suggested: en realidad no nos bastan los estados mágicos sin más: necesitamos estados mágicos *codificados*.
examples.why: Without 'just', the first clause says we do not need magic states at all, which contradicts the rest of the section.

examples.line_approx: Esto podría ser un desafío para algunos códigos
examples.source: This could actually be challenging for some codes selected to make it so
examples.translation: Esto podría ser un desafío para algunos códigos
examples.suggested: Esto podría ser difícil para algunos códigos elegidos precisamente para que lo sea
examples.why: Drops the caveat that the difficulty only shows up for codes chosen on purpose to make it hard, so the claim sounds more general than it is.

examples.source: (or, perhaps more accurately, to make them better)
examples.translation: (o, más precisamente, de mejorarlos)
examples.suggested: (o, quizá con más precisión, de mejorarlos)
examples.why: The hedge 'perhaps' is dropped, which makes a tentative remark sound definite.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The algorithm steps, the Z_f versus Z_OR cost comparison and the search procedure (t = O(√N), "siempre que exista una") are all correct, and the terms are consistent (puerta de consulta de fase, retroceso de fase, qubit auxiliar, tú-imperative "Observa"). A native editor would still fix three small things. "No tiene dependencia de la función f" [16] is a calque. "Estado cero" [20] drops the "all-" of "all-zero state". "Discusión"/"discutimos" [3] is used for "discuss", where "analizar"/"comentar" reads more naturally.

examples.source: Notice that the operation Z_OR has no dependence on the function f
examples.translation: Observa que $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ no tiene dependencia de la función $f$
examples.suggested: Observa que $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ no depende de la función $f$
examples.why: Calque of the English noun phrase; a native writer would use the verb 'depender'.

examples.source: to the all-zero state |0^n⟩
examples.translation: en el estado cero $\vert 0^n \rangle$
examples.suggested: en el estado de todos ceros $\vert 0^n \rangle$
examples.why: 'Estado cero' loses the 'all-' in 'all-zero'. The formula makes the meaning clear, but the conventional rendering keeps it.

examples.source: We'll begin by discussing phase query gates ... we'll briefly discuss how
examples.translation: Comenzamos con la discusión de las *puertas de consulta de fase* ... discutimos brevemente cómo
examples.suggested: Comenzamos analizando las *puertas de consulta de fase* ... comentamos brevemente cómo
examples.why: 'Discusión/discutir' for 'discuss' is a common anglicism in Spanish technical prose. 'Analizar/comentar' is more idiomatic.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the gate counts (7, 10, 21, 9n-5, 5n-3), the Big-O definitions, the number field sieve caveat and the uniformity section. Terminology is consistent (compuerta, semisumador/sumador completo, cribado del cuerpo numérico, MCD). examples.source: as was already mentioned
examples.translation: como ya se menciónó
examples.suggested: como ya se mencionó
examples.why: Spelling error: there is a stray accent on 'menciónó'.

examples.source: doesn't get overwritten after the measurement takes place by another measurement
examples.translation: no se sobreescribe después de que se realice la medición mediante otra medición
examples.suggested: no se sobrescribe mediante otra medición después de realizada la primera

examples.source: binary method and repeated squaring
examples.translation: método binario y cuadrado repetido
examples.suggested: método binario o elevación al cuadrado repetida (exponenciación por cuadrados)

examples.source: an abstract proxy for the time required
examples.translation: un proxy abstracto del tiempo requerido
examples.suggested: una medida indirecta (abstracta) del tiempo requerido
examples.why: 'proxy' is an unnecessary anglicism here. Spanish technical prose would normally say 'medida sustitutiva' or 'medida indirecta'.

examples.source: known algorithms for integer factorization are much more expensive
examples.translation: los algoritmos clásicos conocidos para la factorización entera son mucho más costosos
examples.suggested: los algoritmos conocidos para la factorización entera son mucho más costosos

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The oracle/black-box framing, the unit-cost caveat, the promise problems and the permutation-matrix argument all match the English, and puerta de consulta, oráculo and cómputo are used consistently. The problems are small wording slips. "Don't care" inputs is rendered as entradas "sin importar", which is awkward. In [7] "modelo de consultas de cómputo" is a calque and does not match the title's "modelo de cómputo por consultas". In [29] "la función de entrada $f$ se accede" is ungrammatical and should be "se accede a la función". In [17] a comma has slipped inside the math span ("es decir$,m=1$").

examples.source: are considered as "don't care" inputs
examples.translation: se consideran entradas "sin importar"
examples.suggested: se consideran entradas indiferentes ("don't care")
examples.why: 'sin importar' is not a natural noun modifier. 'Indiferentes' is the usual Spanish term for don't-care inputs in logic and complexity theory.

examples.source: In the *query model* of computation
examples.translation: En el *modelo de consultas* de cómputo
examples.suggested: En el *modelo de cómputo por consultas*
examples.why: This is a calque of the English word order, and it does not match the page title's rendering of the same term.

examples.source: the input function $f$ is accessed through these gates
examples.translation: la función de entrada $f$ se accede a través de estas puertas
examples.suggested: se accede a la función de entrada $f$ a través de estas puertas
examples.why: 'Acceder' takes 'a', so it cannot form a passive with 'se' like this. As written the sentence is ungrammatical.

examples.source: (so $m=1$ for this problem)
examples.translation: (es decir$,m=1$ para este problema)
examples.suggested: (es decir, $m=1$ para este problema)
examples.why: The comma was moved inside the math span, so it renders as part of the formula and the space after 'decir' is lost.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The promise, the two-to-one case, the null-space argument, the 1 - 2^{-r} bound and the exponential classical lower bound all match the English, and the informal tú register holds ("Observa", "imagina"). The problems are calques and stiff wording. "In words" became "En palabras" (twice). "sabor similar" is a calque. "sumaciones" should be "sumatorias". "que la función evalúe a" and "la salida de la función f se aplica XOR sobre" read awkwardly. In [70], "se le suma el vector" (for "it's joined by the vector") is risky in a linear-algebra passage because a learner could read it as vector addition, so "se le une" would be clearer.

examples.source: the all-zero vector is always in the null space of $M$, and it's joined by the vector whose entries are the bits of $s$
examples.translation: el vector de todos ceros siempre está en el espacio nulo de $M$, y en el caso de que $s\neq 0^n$ se le suma el vector cuyas entradas son los bits de $s$
examples.suggested: ...y, en el caso de que $s\neq 0^n$, se le une el vector cuyas entradas son los bits de $s$
examples.why: In a vector-space context, 'se le suma' reads like vector addition rather than 'joins it in the set'. 'se le une' removes the ambiguity.

examples.source: In words, the measurements result in a string $y$ chosen uniformly at random.
examples.translation: En palabras, las mediciones resultan en una cadena $y\in\Sigma^n$ elegida uniformemente al azar.
examples.suggested: Dicho de otro modo, las mediciones dan como resultado una cadena $y\in\Sigma^n$ elegida uniformemente al azar.
examples.why: 'En palabras' and 'resultan en' are calques of English phrasing. The same pattern appears again in [57].

examples.source: the output of the function $f$ is XORed onto the all-zero state of the bottom $m$ qubits
examples.translation: la salida de la función $f$ se aplica XOR sobre el estado de todos ceros de los $m$ qubits inferiores
examples.suggested: se aplica el XOR de la salida de la función $f$ sobre el estado de todos ceros de los $m$ qubits inferiores
examples.why: As written, the output itself 'is applied XOR', which is ungrammatical and reads as machine translation.

examples.source: represented exactly once by the two summations
examples.translation: representada exactamente una vez por las dos sumaciones
examples.suggested: representada exactamente una vez en las dos sumatorias
examples.why: 'sumatorias' (or 'sumas') is the standard Spanish mathematical term. 'sumaciones' is unusual.

examples.source: a promise problem with a flavor similar to the Deutsch-Jozsa and Bernstein-Vazirani problems
examples.translation: un problema de promesa con un sabor similar a los problemas de Deutsch-Jozsa y Bernstein-Vazirani
examples.suggested: un problema de promesa de naturaleza similar a los problemas de Deutsch-Jozsa y Bernstein-Vazirani
examples.why: 'sabor' is a literal calque of 'flavor'. A native technical writer would write 'naturaleza' or 'estilo'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The trace and positive semidefinite definitions, the caveat that P≥0 is not entrywise nonnegativity, the global-phase argument and the faithful-representation claim all match the English. The problems are small slips. [55] has a typo, "identicos" for "idénticos". In [30], "Cómo funcionan e interpretan las matrices" is ungrammatical because it drops the reflexive "se interpretan". [31] says "medición de la base estándar", but [52] uses the correct "medición en la base estándar". "Positive semidefiniteness" appears both as "semidefinitud positiva" ([11], [23]) and as the awkward "la propiedad semidefinida positiva" ([27]). "Traza unitaria" in [10] could be misread as a reference to unitarity.

examples.source: The way density matrices work and can be interpreted will be clarified as the lesson continues
examples.translation: Cómo funcionan e interpretan las matrices de densidad se aclarará a lo largo de la lección
examples.suggested: Cómo funcionan las matrices de densidad y cómo se interpretan se aclarará a lo largo de la lección
examples.why: The coordinated verb has no reflexive 'se', so it reads as if the matrices interpret something. This is ungrammatical and awkward.

examples.source: if we perform a standard basis measurement
examples.translation: en una medición de la base estándar
examples.suggested: en una medición en la base estándar
examples.why: This is inconsistent with [52]. A measurement is made 'en' a basis; 'medición de la base' reads as measuring the basis itself.

examples.source: two quantum states are identical
examples.translation: dos estados cuánticos son identicos
examples.suggested: dos estados cuánticos son idénticos
examples.why: The written accent is missing, a spelling error.

examples.source: matches the definition of positive semidefiniteness
examples.translation: corresponde a la definición de la propiedad semidefinida positiva
examples.suggested: corresponde a la definición de semidefinitud positiva
examples.why: Elsewhere in the file ([11], [23]) this is 'semidefinitud positiva'. This paraphrase is inconsistent and clunky.

examples.source: Unit trace
examples.translation: Traza unitaria
examples.suggested: Traza igual a 1 (o traza unidad)
examples.why: 'Unitaria' suggests a unitary matrix to a quantum learner. 'Traza igual a 1' is clearer.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The Helstrom–Holevo result, the Holevo-Yuen-Kennedy-Lax "si y solo si" condition, the adaptive vs. non-adaptive strategies and the rounding caveats in [76] and [96] all keep their sense. Entry [75] has two accent errors a native editor would fix: "En el limite" should be "límite", and "está aproximación" should be the demonstrative "esta aproximación", not the verb. There are also two small dropped qualifiers: [36] loses "respectively" and [59] turns "closely approximates" into just "se aproxime".

examples.source: In the limit as $N$ approaches infinity, this approximation converges in probability
examples.translation: En el limite, cuando $N$ tiende a infinito, está aproximación converge en probabilidad
examples.suggested: En el límite, cuando $N$ tiende a infinito, esta aproximación converge en probabilidad
examples.why: Two spelling errors. 'limite' is missing its accent, and 'está' (the verb) is used where the demonstrative 'esta' is needed. Readers notice these in teaching material.

examples.source: to compute a density matrix $\tilde{\rho}$ that closely approximates $\rho$
examples.translation: calcular una matriz de densidad $\tilde{\rho}$ que se aproxime a $\rho$
examples.suggested: calcular una matriz de densidad $\tilde{\rho}$ que se aproxime bien a $\rho$
examples.why: The qualifier 'closely' is dropped. This is a small weakening of the goal as stated and does not mislead.

examples.source: for $P_0$ and $P_1$, respectively
examples.translation: para $P_0$ y $P_1$
examples.suggested: para $P_0$ y $P_1$, respectivamente
examples.why: 'Respectively' is dropped. The word order still implies the pairing, so this is only a minor loss of precision.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. The most visible defect is the IBMVideo title in [5], which is in German ("In diesem Video implementiert…") on the Spanish page. "Overlap" is translated as "superposición" in [22], [31] and [50]. In [22] the same word also means quantum superposition ("la superposición de estados base"), so the two ideas blur; "solapamiento" is the clearer term. Smaller points: "If these are sampled at all" becomes "de alguna manera" ("somehow"), "tend to be" is dropped in [64], "primitivos" should be "primitivas", and [99] has the calque "hemos trabajado a través de".

examples.source: In this video, Iskandar Sitdikov implements a hybrid classical quantum calculation using a simulated HPC environment.
examples.translation: In diesem Video implementiert Iskandar Sitdikov eine hybride klassisch-quantenmechanische Berechnung in einer simulierten HPC-Umgebung.
examples.suggested: En este video, Iskandar Sitdikov implementa un cálculo híbrido clásico-cuántico usando un entorno HPC simulado.
examples.why: The video title attribute is in German, not Spanish. It is the wrong language and a reader will see it.

examples.source: should ideally have a large overlap with the support of the true ground state
examples.translation: idealmente debería tener una gran superposición con el soporte del verdadero estado fundamental
examples.suggested: idealmente debería tener un gran solapamiento con el soporte del verdadero estado fundamental
examples.why: This paragraph also uses 'superposición' for quantum superposition, so 'overlap' and 'superposition' end up as the same word. 'Solapamiento' is unambiguous. The same change applies in [31] and [50].

examples.source: If these are sampled at all, even if their overlap with our ansatz is small
examples.translation: Si estas se muestrean de alguna manera —incluso si su superposición con nuestro ansatz es pequeña—
examples.suggested: Si estas se muestrean aunque sea una vez —incluso si su solapamiento con nuestro ansatz es pequeño—
examples.why: 'At all' means 'even once', which is the point about noise robustness. 'De alguna manera' means 'somehow' and loses that.

examples.source: the Hamiltonians for spin lattices tend to be more compactly expressible in Pauli matrices
examples.translation: los hamiltonianos para redes de espín se expresan de forma más compacta en matrices de Pauli
examples.suggested: los hamiltonianos para redes de espín suelen expresarse de forma más compacta en matrices de Pauli
examples.why: Dropping 'tend to' turns a general tendency into an absolute claim.

examples.source: a task that uses primitives to execute our quantum circuit
examples.translation: una tarea que utiliza primitivos para ejecutar nuestro circuito cuántico
examples.suggested: una tarea que utiliza primitivas para ejecutar nuestro circuito cuántico
examples.why: Spanish Qiskit material usually uses the feminine 'primitivas' for Sampler/Estimator.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The fermionic-to-bosonic mapping rationale, the Qiskit ZZII qubit-ordering explanation and the active-space selection (6th to 10th orbitals) all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few small things. [41] renders "electronic core" as "núcleo electrónico", which sits close to "repulsión nuclear" and could be misread as the atomic nucleus. [66] uses the stiff passive calque "son afectados por el operador identidad". [36] "multi-configuración" should be the conventional "multiconfiguracional", and [13] "soluciones prediseñadas" should be "preempaquetadas".

examples.source: separated into energy of an electronic core (ecore, not involved in minimization)
examples.translation: se divide en la energía del núcleo electrónico (ecore, no participa en la minimización)
examples.suggested: se divide en la energía del core electrónico (electrones internos; ecore, que no participa en la minimización)
examples.why: 'núcleo' clashes with 'repulsión nuclear' used nearby. The chemistry sense of core (inner, frozen electrons) is clearer as 'core' or 'electrones internos'.

examples.source: qubits 0 and 1 being acting on by the identity operator, qubits 2 and 3 being acted on by the Z operator, ordered with qubit 0 furthest to the right
examples.translation: los qubits 0 y 1 son afectados por el operador identidad, los qubits 2 y 3 por el operador Z, con el qubit 0 a la derecha
examples.suggested: el operador identidad actúa sobre los qubits 0 y 1 y el operador Z sobre los qubits 2 y 3, con el qubit 0 en el extremo derecho
examples.why: The passive 'son afectados por' is a calque; 'actúa sobre' is the normal idiom. Dropping 'furthest' also makes the ordering convention less precise.

examples.source: a multi-configuration self-consistent fields package
examples.translation: un paquete de campos autoconsistentes multi-configuración
examples.suggested: un paquete de campo autoconsistente multiconfiguracional (MCSCF)
examples.why: The conventional Spanish term is 'multiconfiguracional'. The hyphenated noun used as an adjective reads like a calque.

examples.source: the process of Hamiltonian preparation transfers to prepackaged solutions as well
examples.translation: el proceso de preparación del hamiltoniano también se puede trasladar a soluciones prediseñadas
examples.suggested: el proceso de preparación del hamiltoniano también es aplicable a soluciones preempaquetadas
examples.why: 'prediseñadas' means pre-designed, not packaged off-the-shelf software. 'preempaquetadas' or 'ya empaquetadas' is closer.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and the core terms are consistent (compuertas, hamiltoniano, qubits auxiliares, recuperación de configuración, solucionador de estados propios). No sentence would mislead a learner, but a few phrasings are stiff or calqued. In [31], "2 up- and 2 down-spin" became the broken "2 hacia arriba y 2 hacia abajo-espín". In [40], "every other orbital" was calqued as "Cada segundo orbital". In [39], the ordinal "4-to" is malformed. "Flip" is rendered as both "voltear" ([68]) and "invertir/inversión" (everywhere else), and "pass manager" is capitalized as "Pass Manager" in [49] but not in [54]–[56].

examples.source: for 4 spatial orbitals and 2 up- and 2 down-spin may look like the following
examples.translation: para 4 orbitales espaciales y 2 hacia arriba y 2 hacia abajo-espín puede verse como sigue
examples.suggested: para 4 orbitales espaciales con 2 electrones de espín arriba y 2 de espín abajo podría verse así
examples.why: Ungrammatical hyphenated calque; the electrons being counted are left unnamed.

examples.source: Every other orbital, such as 0th, 2nd, and 4th indexed orbitals, becomes nearest neighbors
examples.translation: Cada segundo orbital, por ejemplo el 0.o, 2.o y 4.o orbital indexado, se convierte en vecino más cercano
examples.suggested: Uno de cada dos orbitales (por ejemplo, los de índice 0, 2 y 4) pasan a ser vecinos más cercanos
examples.why: 'Cada segundo' calques 'every other'. A native writer would say 'uno de cada dos' or 'orbitales alternos'.

examples.source: kept between every $4$-th indexed (such as the 0th, 4th, and 8th) spin orbitals
examples.translation: se mantienen entre cada $4$-to orbital de espín indexado
examples.suggested: se mantienen cada cuatro orbitales de espín (por ejemplo, los de índice 0, 4 y 8)
examples.why: '4-to' is not a valid Spanish ordinal abbreviation (4.º), and the structure is calqued.

examples.source: The probability of flipping can be ... a weighted probability of flipping
examples.translation: La probabilidad de voltear puede ser ... una probabilidad de voltear ponderada
examples.suggested: La probabilidad de inversión puede ser ... una probabilidad de inversión ponderada
examples.why: Everywhere else the file renders 'flip' as invertir/inversión. 'Voltear' here breaks that consistency.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, and the page is otherwise faithful: qubit, puerta, mapa de acoplamiento and Target are used correctly and in the tú register. In [28], the second comparison drops the hedge: "tend to be larger" becomes "son mayores", which states the 2-qubit vs 1-qubit error ordering as a firm rule. In [17], "pares pueden conectarse directamente con la puerta" loosely paraphrases "pairs to which you can directly apply the gate". Two terms are inconsistent within the file: the heading says "Coupling Map" but the body says "mapa de acoplamiento", and the platform is "IBM Quantum Platform" in [21] but "Plataforma IBM Quantum" in [29].

examples.source: which in turn tend to be larger than the 1-qubit operation
examples.translation: que a su vez son mayores que los errores de las operaciones de 1 qubit
examples.suggested: que a su vez suelen ser mayores que los de las operaciones de 1 qubit
examples.why: Drops the 'tend to' qualifier, which turns a typical trend into a firm claim.

examples.source: Edges indicate pairs to which you can directly apply the 2-qubit entangling gate.
examples.translation: Las aristas indican qué pares pueden conectarse directamente con la puerta de entrelazamiento de 2 qubits.
examples.suggested: Las aristas indican los pares a los que se puede aplicar directamente la puerta de entrelazamiento de 2 qubits.
examples.why: 'Conectarse con la puerta' is a loose paraphrase. The point is that the gate can be applied directly to those pairs.

examples.source: 2.2 Coupling map
examples.translation: 2.2 Coupling Map
examples.suggested: 2.2 Mapa de acoplamiento
examples.why: The heading keeps the English term while the body in [17] uses 'mapa de acoplamiento'. That is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Platform
examples.translation: Plataforma IBM Quantum
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Platform
examples.why: [21] keeps the product name 'IBM Quantum Platform', but [29] translates it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and core terms are correct and consistent (hamiltoniano, puertas de rotación, pasos de Trotter, mapa de acoplamiento, colorear). The problems are small ones. Entry [24] has a spelling error ("menciónó"). Entry [42] turns "we do not (should not) ask the transpiler" into the clumsy "no debe (__no__) volver a realizar". Entry [27] changes "random use" to "primer uso". Entry [68] makes two claims softer: "higher fidelity" becomes "mayor precisión", and "quantum lead time" becomes just "esa ventaja". "Fake device" is written three ways: "dispositivo simulado (fake device)", "Fake Device" and "fake device".

examples.source: As mentioned above, we focus on the RZZ gate
examples.translation: Como se menciónó anteriormente
examples.suggested: Como se mencionó anteriormente
examples.why: Spelling error: 'mencionó' needs only one accent mark.

examples.source: we do not (__should not__) ask the transpiler to do qubit mapping and routing
examples.translation: el transpilador no debe (__no__) volver a realizar el mapeo de qubits ni el enrutamiento
examples.suggested: no le pedimos (y __no debemos__ pedirle) al transpilador que realice el mapeo de qubits ni el enrutamiento
examples.why: The bold parenthetical '(no)' after 'no debe' is awkward. It also loses the contrast between what we do and what we should do.

examples.source: faster, with higher fidelity, or more cheaply ... until at some point that quantum lead time becomes critically important
examples.translation: más rápido, con mayor precisión o de forma más económica ... hasta que esa ventaja se vuelva decisivamente importante
examples.suggested: con mayor fidelidad ... hasta que esa ventaja temporal cuántica se vuelva de importancia crítica
examples.why: In quantum computing, 'fidelity' is a technical term and is not the same as 'precisión'. 'Lead time' means the time head start, and 'esa ventaja' drops that meaning. It does not mislead, but it is less precise than the English.

examples.source: Let us make a random use of the newly-defined `rzz`.
examples.translation: Hagamos un primer uso del `rzz` recién definido.
examples.suggested: Usemos el `rzz` recién definido en un ejemplo arbitrario.
examples.why: 'random use' (an arbitrary trial use) became 'first use'. This is a small change of meaning.

examples.source: Optimize and execute (fake device)
examples.translation: Optimizar y ejecutar (Fake Device)
examples.suggested: Optimizar y ejecutar (dispositivo simulado)
examples.why: 'Fake device' appears as 'dispositivo simulado (fake device)' in [18]/[47], as 'Fake Device' here and as 'fake device' in [54]. The term should be written one way throughout.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the max-cut and QUBO derivation, the z_i substitution, the Estimator vs Sampler guidance and the noise caveat in [115], so nothing here would mislead a learner. 'Ground state' is rendered as the calque 'estado base' throughout. Spanish physics texts normally say 'estado fundamental'. QAOA's expanded name varies between 'algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada' ([11]) and 'Algoritmo de Optimización Aproximada Cuántica' ([37], [38], [116]). Two smaller slips: [24] drops 'very' ('a very low-energy state' becomes 'un estado de baja energía'), and [91] moves the period inside the link text ('[documentación.]').

examples.source: a Hamiltonian for which the ground state corresponds to the solution
examples.translation: un Hamiltoniano cuyo estado base corresponde a la solución
examples.suggested: un Hamiltoniano cuyo estado fundamental corresponde a la solución
examples.why: 'Estado fundamental' is the standard Spanish physics term for ground state. 'Estado base' is a recognizable calque, and it appears in [53], [74] and [77] as well.

examples.source: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)
examples.translation: Algoritmo de Optimización Aproximada Cuántica (QAOA)
examples.suggested: algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada (QAOA)
examples.why: This does not match the rendering in [11]. The adjective order 'Optimización Aproximada Cuántica' also makes 'cuántica' modify 'optimización' rather than the algorithm.

examples.source: did not correspond to a very low-energy (or low-eigenvalue) state
examples.translation: no corresponden a un estado de baja energía (o bajo valor propio)
examples.suggested: no correspondían a un estado de muy baja energía (o de valor propio bajo)
examples.why: The qualifier 'very' is dropped and the tense shifts from past to present. This is a small nuance loss, not a misleading change.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and the key terms are rendered consistently: "wire cut" as "corte de hilo", "sampling overhead" as "costo de muestreo" and "subobservables" as "subobservables". The limit of "un máximo de 4 qubits por subcircuito" matches the source exactly.

The meaning is faithful throughout, including the caveats on monotonicity in [39]/[40] and the reason for scaling to 0.0 in [54], so a learner would not be misled. There are still some consistency and calque slips. "Shot" appears as "disparo" in [3] but as "shots" in [27]/[30]. The section headings switch between infinitives ("Generar…", "Aplicar twirling…") and tú imperatives ("Aprende el ruido", "Propaga…", "Muestrea…"). "Left-dressed" in [16] is calqued as "vestido izquierdo", "noise learner" in [27] as "aprendiz de ruido" and "Bindings" in [52] as "Ligaduras", and "allow it to grow large" in [43] loses "large" ("permitir que crezca").

examples.source: reflecting every shot for every twirling randomization
examples.translation: que reflejen cada disparo para cada aleatorización de twirling
examples.suggested: que reflejen cada shot para cada aleatorización de twirling
examples.why: Entries [27] and [30] keep 'shots' in English. Pick one rendering for the whole file.

examples.source: Single qubit gates will be left-dressed within the boxes.
examples.translation: Las compuertas de un solo qubit se incluirán como vestido izquierdo dentro de las cajas.
examples.suggested: Las compuertas de un solo qubit se agregarán a la izquierda (left-dressed) dentro de las cajas.
examples.why: 'Vestido izquierdo' is a literal calque that reads as nonsense. Keeping the English term in parentheses makes it recognizable.

examples.source: Learn the noise
examples.translation: Aprende el ruido
examples.suggested: Aprender el ruido
examples.why: Other headings ([6], [14], [22]) use infinitives, while [25], [34], [36], [45], [48], [57] and [59] use imperatives. The headings should use one form throughout.

examples.source: it is often still useful to allow it to grow large
examples.translation: a menudo sigue siendo útil permitir que crezca
examples.suggested: a menudo sigue siendo útil permitir que crezca mucho
examples.why: Drops 'large'. The point is that Õ should become large, not merely grow. This is a small loss of emphasis, not a misleading change.

examples.source: Bindings necessary to fully define the samplex
examples.translation: Ligaduras necesarias para definir completamente el samplex
examples.suggested: Asignaciones (bindings) necesarias para definir completamente el samplex
examples.why: In Spanish, 'ligaduras' means physical constraints or ties. It is not the usual term for parameter bindings.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The shock-validity condition in [36], the inviscid/viscous framing in [30]-[31] and the HDES vs. PINN parameter and iteration counts in [45]-[49] all match the English. The main defect is register: the page mostly uses tú, but slips into usted in [0] "Utilice", [17] "asegúrese", [40] "esté intentando", [41] "puede ver", [42] "puede desactivarlos" and [57] "tómese… Sus opiniones". There are also a few calques. [6] has "podrías querer dividir" and a redundant "tú lo lees". [8] has "QPUs Heron R2 de 156Q".

examples.source: Use the QUICK-PDE function to model a flowing non-viscous fluid.
examples.translation: Utilice la función QUICK-PDE para modelar un fluido no viscoso en movimiento.
examples.suggested: Usa la función QUICK-PDE para modelar un fluido no viscoso en movimiento.
examples.why: Formal usted imperative; the page convention is informal tú.

examples.source: Depending on the configuration you're trying to solve, the algorithm's parameters ... might need to be adapted
examples.translation: Dependiendo de la configuración que esté intentando resolver, los parámetros del algoritmo ... podrían necesitar ser adaptados
examples.suggested: Según la configuración que intentes resolver, quizá haya que adaptar los parámetros del algoritmo
examples.why: Uses usted, and 'podrían necesitar ser adaptados' is a passive calque of the English.

examples.source: Please take a minute to provide feedback on this tutorial. Your insights will help us...
examples.translation: Por favor, tómese un minuto para proporcionar comentarios sobre este tutorial. Sus opiniones nos ayudarán...
examples.suggested: Tómate un minuto para darnos tu opinión sobre este tutorial. Tus comentarios nos ayudarán...
examples.why: Formal register, which is inconsistent with the tú used elsewhere on the page.

examples.source: so you might want to split this tutorial in two sections: the first one, in which you read through it and launch the jobs
examples.translation: por lo que podrías querer dividir este tutorial en dos secciones: la primera, en la que tú lo lees y lanzas los trabajos
examples.suggested: por lo que quizá te convenga dividir este tutorial en dos partes: la primera, en la que lo lees y lanzas los trabajos
examples.why: 'podrías querer' is a calque of 'might want to', and the explicit 'tú' is redundant in Spanish.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and the terms are consistent: compuertas, mapa de acoplamiento, gestor de pasadas, evaluación comparativa aleatorizada (RB), disparos. The main problem is register. The page switches between tú and usted: [0] "Ejecuta ... y actualice", [4] "Su tiempo", [45] "Si observa ... inspecciónelas ... intente" and [53] "responda ... Sus opiniones". [45] also has a grammatical slip, "la rutina de ajusta", which should be "la rutina de ajuste". [51] ends on the calque "en tales instancias".

examples.source: If you see warnings coming from these experiments, inspect them ... and try adjusting
examples.translation: Si observa advertencias provenientes de estos experimentos, inspecciónelas ... e intente ajustar
examples.suggested: Si ves advertencias de estos experimentos, inspecciónalas ... e intenta ajustar
examples.why: This uses the formal usted, while the rest of the file (and the same sentence's 'Ten en cuenta') uses tú.

examples.source: when the fitting routine cannot fit a curve
examples.translation: cuando la rutina de ajusta no puede ajustar una curva
examples.suggested: cuando la rutina de ajuste no puede ajustar una curva a los datos medidos
examples.why: 'de ajusta' is a verb form where a noun is needed, so the phrase is ungrammatical.

examples.source: Run real-time characterization experiments and update backend properties
examples.translation: Ejecuta experimentos de caracterización en tiempo real y actualice las propiedades del backend
examples.suggested: Ejecuta experimentos de caracterización en tiempo real y actualiza las propiedades del backend
examples.why: The sentence starts in tú ('Ejecuta') and switches to usted ('actualice').

examples.source: Please take this short survey ... Your insights will help us
examples.translation: Por favor, responda esta breve encuesta ... Sus opiniones nos ayudarán
examples.suggested: Responde esta breve encuesta ... Tus opiniones nos ayudarán
examples.why: This is formal usted, but the page convention is informal tú.

examples.source: help us avoid experimental failures in such instances
examples.translation: ayudarnos a evitar fallas experimentales en tales instancias
examples.suggested: ayudarnos a evitar fallos experimentales en esos casos
examples.why: 'en tales instancias' is a calque of 'in such instances'; 'en esos casos' is how a native writer would say it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The variational-principle caveat ("cota superior"), the two-evaluations-per-iteration claim for SPSA, the barren-plateau explanation ("mesetas áridas") and the SQD comparison all match the source, and the core terms (hamiltoniano, ansatz, valor esperado, estado fundamental, backend) are used consistently. A native editor would still fix four calqued phrases: the heading "Introduciendo SPSA" (should be "Introducción a SPSA"), "uno de los optimizadores más preferidos", "programa de tasa de aprendizaje" for "learning rate schedule", and the English-style passive opening "Un ejemplo a gran escala en hardware no está incluido en este tutorial".

examples.source: Introducing SPSA
examples.translation: Introduciendo SPSA
examples.suggested: Introducción a SPSA
examples.why: A gerund heading copies the English form; Spanish technical headings use a noun phrase.

examples.source: It is, therefore, one of the highly preferred optimizers for implementing variational algorithms.
examples.translation: Por ello, es uno de los optimizadores más preferidos para implementar algoritmos variacionales.
examples.suggested: Por ello, es uno de los optimizadores preferidos para implementar algoritmos variacionales.
examples.why: "Preferido" already means the top choice, so "más preferidos" sounds awkward to a native reader.

examples.source: Adjust the learning rate schedule parameters
examples.translation: Ajusta los parámetros del programa de tasa de aprendizaje
examples.suggested: Ajusta los parámetros del esquema de la tasa de aprendizaje
examples.why: "Programa" is a literal rendering of "schedule". "Esquema" (or "calendario") de la tasa de aprendizaje is the usual phrasing in Spanish ML texts. The sentence also repeats "Ajusta" in the heading and the body.

examples.source: A large-scale hardware example is not included in this tutorial.
examples.translation: Un ejemplo a gran escala en hardware no está incluido en este tutorial.
examples.suggested: Este tutorial no incluye un ejemplo a gran escala en hardware.
examples.why: The passive construction follows English word order; an active verb reads more naturally in Spanish.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The terms are correct and used consistently: hamiltoniano, cúbit, compuertas RZZ, valor esperado, trotterizados, dimensión de enlace, disparos. The file slips into formal usted in two places: "Su tiempo de ejecución" in [4], and "tómese" and "Sus opiniones" in the survey text in [58]. In [7], "entangling two-qubit interactions" becomes just "acoplamientos de dos cúbits", which drops the idea of entanglement. [7] also has the redundant "diseño avanzado de layout", and [50] has the calque "ejecución con reconocimiento de ruido" for "noise-aware execution".

examples.source: Your runtime may vary.
examples.translation: Su tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.suggested: Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.why: Formal usted slip. The project convention is informal tú.

examples.source: Please take a minute to provide feedback on this tutorial. Your insights will help us...
examples.translation: Por favor, tómese un minuto ... Sus opiniones nos ayudarán...
examples.suggested: Tómate un minuto para darnos tu opinión sobre este tutorial. Tus comentarios nos ayudarán...
examples.why: Formal imperative and possessive. The rest of the page uses tú.

examples.source: alternate between single-qubit rotations and entangling two-qubit interactions ... advanced layout, routing
examples.translation: alternan entre rotaciones de un solo cúbit y acoplamientos de dos cúbits ... diseño avanzado de layout, enrutamiento
examples.suggested: alternan entre rotaciones de un solo cúbit e interacciones entrelazantes de dos cúbits ... layout avanzado, enrutamiento
examples.why: The translation drops 'entangling', which is the point of these interactions. 'diseño avanzado de layout' says layout twice.

examples.source: while Fire Opal handles the noise-aware execution
examples.translation: mientras Fire Opal se encarga de la ejecución con reconocimiento de ruido
examples.suggested: mientras Fire Opal se encarga de una ejecución que tiene en cuenta el ruido
examples.why: 'con reconocimiento de ruido' is a stiff calque of '-aware'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The criteria, the GHZ, T1 and Toffoli examples, the readout-error percentages and the teleportation mapping to criteria 6 and 7 all match the English, and nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are stylistic. Several phrases are calqued: "comiencen con una pizarra en blanco" for "clean slate", "efectivamente 'enviándolo'", "Siéntete libre de extender" and "¡feliz computación cuántica!". "Feed-forward control" becomes the non-standard "control de avance", and "unitario de múltiples qubits" uses "unitario" as a bare noun. "Reliable" switches between "fiable" in [14] and "confiable" in [57] and [77], and the heading in [66] has odd capitalization: "(qubits Voladores)".

examples.source: so that algorithms begin on a clean slate
examples.translation: para que los algoritmos comiencen con una pizarra en blanco
examples.suggested: para que los algoritmos partan desde cero / de un estado limpio
examples.why: Literal calque of an English idiom; a Spanish technical writer would not phrase it this way.

examples.source: feed-forward control in action
examples.translation: el control de avance en acción
examples.suggested: el control feed-forward (prealimentado) en acción
examples.why: 'Control de avance' is not a recognized term for feed-forward, so learners can't map it to the concept.

examples.source: effectively 'sending' it to Bob
examples.translation: efectivamente 'enviándolo' a Bob
examples.suggested: 'enviándolo' en la práctica a Bob / en efecto, 'enviándolo' a Bob
examples.why: In Spanish, 'efectivamente' means 'indeed', so this is a false-friend calque.

examples.source: any multi-qubit unitary can be composed
examples.translation: cualquier unitario de múltiples qubits puede componerse
examples.suggested: cualquier operación unitaria de múltiples qubits puede componerse
examples.why: Using 'unitario' as a bare noun is an anglicism; the usual Spanish form is 'operación unitaria'.

examples.source: Feel free to extend these experiments, and happy quantum computing!
examples.translation: Siéntete libre de extender estos experimentos, ¡y feliz computación cuántica!
examples.suggested: Anímate a ampliar estos experimentos. ¡Disfruta de la computación cuántica!
examples.why: Both clauses are word-for-word English formulas.

examples.source: Quantum Communication Criteria (Flying Qubits)
examples.translation: Criterios de Comunicación Cuántica (qubits Voladores)
examples.suggested: Criterios de comunicación cuántica (qubits voladores)
examples.why: The capitalization is inconsistent: English title case is kept, but 'qubits' is lowercased while 'Voladores' is capitalized.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The T1 decay explanation, the Toffoli decomposition and the teleportation mapping to criteria 6 and 7 are all correct, and the source's own out-of-order criterion numbering in [12] is kept as it is. The problems are consistency and polish. "Quantum computer" switches between "computadora cuántica" ([0], [4], [21], [22], [24]) and "ordenador cuántico" ([36], [61], [63], [78]), so the cross-reference in [61] no longer matches the heading in [21]. "Notebook" becomes "cuaderno" in [79], "Demo" alternates with "demostración", and "resetear" alternates with "reinicios". There is also an agreement error in [61] ("Los datos ... lista"), "feed-forward" is rendered as "retroalimentación" (which means feedback) in [68], and the capitalisation in the headings [13] and [62] is odd ("qubits Escalables", "qubits Voladores").

examples.source: Running on a real device was demonstrated in **Exercise 1b: Run on real IBM Quantum computer**.
examples.translation: La ejecución en un dispositivo real se demostró en el **Ejercicio 1b: Ejecutar en un ordenador IBM Quantum real**.
examples.suggested: ... en el **Ejercicio 1b: Ejecutar en una computadora IBM Quantum real**.
examples.why: The heading in [21] uses 'computadora'. The file mixes computadora and ordenador for 'quantum computer', so this cross-reference no longer matches the heading it points to.

examples.source: The device calibration data lists a readout error for each qubit.
examples.translation: Los datos de calibración del dispositivo lista un error de lectura para cada qubit.
examples.suggested: Los datos de calibración del dispositivo listan un error de lectura para cada qubit.
examples.why: The subject is plural ('Los datos'), so the verb must be plural too.

examples.source: feed-forward control in action
examples.translation: el control de retroalimentación en acción
examples.suggested: el control feed-forward (prealimentado) en acción
examples.why: 'Retroalimentación' means feedback, which is not the same idea as classical feed-forward in teleportation. The rendering is still recognizable but inexact.

examples.source: Criterion 1 – Scalable, Well-Characterized Qubits
examples.translation: Criterio 1 – qubits Escalables y Bien Caracterizados
examples.suggested: Criterio 1 – Qubits escalables y bien caracterizados
examples.why: The title case is inverted: the first word is lowercase and the adjectives are capitalized. The same happens in [62] ('qubits Voladores').

examples.source: By completing the exercises in this notebook
examples.translation: Al completar los ejercicios de este cuaderno
examples.suggested: Al completar los ejercicios de este notebook
examples.why: [4] and [11] use 'notebook' but this entry switches to 'cuaderno'. 'Demo' and 'demostración' alternate in the same way ([15] and [27] vs [37] and [43]).
